messages.subject: Curiculum planning
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I would like to organise a first live discussion to discuss a Bioconductor curriculum. I have created a doodle poll for next week with suggestions that should work for all time zones of anticipated participants.

  https://doodle.com/poll/42x582wqaqhe6ixw

It can of course be expanded if needed.

Best wishes,

Laurent

In the meantime, feel free to put any discussion points on the agenda (in the google doc).

messages.subject: Bioc-teaching meeting: Monday 6 July at 5pm CEST
messages.subject_clean: Bioc-teaching meeting: Monday 6 July at 5pm CEST
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

It seems that Monday 6 July at 5pm CEST is the time slot that earns most votes: 7 'yes' + 1 'if need be'. Given that this will be our first meeting, it will be important to get a majority on board for this Bioc curriculum planning kick-off meeting.

I will send meeting details in due time.

Looking forward to meeting you all.

Best wishes,

Laurent

messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Please find the meeting details below. We'll be using (1) Jitsi, an open-source video conferencing solution. Simply click the link below and connect with your browser or download an app for your phone (https://jitsi.org/#download).

Join the meeting: https://meet.jit.si/BioconductorTeaching <https://slack-redir.net/link?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmeet.jit.si%2FBioconductorTeaching&v=3>
To join by phone instead, tap this: +1.512.647.1431,,2105280635#
Looking for a different dial-in number? See meeting dial-in numbers: https://meet.jit.si/static/dialInInfo.html?room=BioconductorTeaching <https://slack-redir.net/link?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmeet.jit.si%2Fstatic%2FdialInInfo.html%3Froom%3DBioconductorTeaching&v=3>
If also dialing-in through a room phone, join without connecting to audio: https://meet.jit.si/BioconductorTeaching#config.startSilent=true <https://slack-redir.net/link?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmeet.jit.si%2FBioconductorTeaching%23config.startSilent%3Dtrue&v=3>

Best wishes,

Laurent

(1) Testing, in my case. But I'm quite keen to test an open-source alternative to the commercial options.
